segments.t: 星期五下午五点刚过，格雷厄姆手里拿着小小的黄铜螺丝刀站在前台后，汉娜和阿瑟正看着他在木制钥匙板上添加新东西。先听一遍吧。
For fifteen years in my hands, that board only held hooks one through eight.
And look on the right edge: there were two tiny screw holes under the varnish all along.
No way! Hook number nine used to hang right there thirty years ago!
One turn, two turns... solid brass hook number nine, back where it belongs.
May I hang the big sunroom key on it, Graham?
Go right ahead, Hannah. You earned it this week.
Wait, Graham, what is that laminated card tucked inside your paper ledger?
Aha! Did you secretly keep a copy of my printed cafe menu, Graham?!
Only because your big numbers are easy to read without a lamp.
Write this day down in the guest book: Graham praised a printed page!
Do not celebrate too much, boss. Paper books still win when it rains.
Look at the courtyard clock: half past five! Let us light the lanterns!
现在，我们放慢节奏，一句一句品味这段对话。
For fifteen years in my hands, that board only held hooks one through eight.
「这块板子在我手里十五年了，上面一直只有一到八号挂钩。」 在美式英语中，要表示从头到尾的完整跨度，介词
one through eight
非常直接地表达了“从一到八包含在内”的意思。
And look on the right edge: there were two tiny screw holes under the varnish all along.
「看这右边边缘：清漆下面其实一直有两个小小的螺丝孔。」 在亮闪闪的
varnish
涂层下面，藏着
screw holes
几个保留着这块木板回忆的螺丝孔。
No way! Hook number nine used to hang right there thirty years ago!
「不会吧！三十年前九号挂钩就挂在那儿！」 用来回忆过去存在但现在已经改变的情况时，句型
used to hang
立刻形成了过去与现在的鲜明对比。
One turn, two turns... solid brass hook number nine, back where it belongs.
「转一圈，转两圈……纯黄铜的九号挂钩，终于回到了它该在的地方。」 这句非常地道生动的表达
back where it belongs
表示某样物品回到了它真正该待的地方。
May I hang the big sunroom key on it, Graham?
「我可以把日光浴室的大钥匙挂上去吗，格雷厄姆？」 比 can 更礼貌、更显尊重的语气词
May I
在向钥匙板的守护者温柔地请求许可。
Go right ahead, Hannah. You earned it this week.
「挂吧，汉娜。这是你这星期赢来的。」 为了亲切地给予对方许可，这个邀请
Go right ahead
还伴随着一个动词
earned
表示凭借自己的努力赢得了某物。
Wait, Graham, what is that laminated card tucked inside your paper ledger?
「等等，格雷厄姆，你那本纸质账本里夹着的是什么过胶卡片？」 被硬质塑料保护起来的纸页被称为
laminated card
而过去分词
tucked inside
生动地描绘了悄悄把它夹在两页之间的动作。
Aha! Did you secretly keep a copy of my printed cafe menu, Graham?!
「哈！你是不是偷偷藏了一份我打印的咖啡馆菜单，格雷厄姆？！」 当我们谈论印刷品的一份，而不是赝品时，会用到
a copy of
这里还结合了可爱的副词
secretly
偷偷地，暗中地。
Only because your big numbers are easy to read without a lamp.
「那只是因为你打印的大字号，不用开灯也能看得很清楚。」 在容易或困难等形容词后面，英语会使用主动形式的不定式，如
easy to read
跟我们的“容易读”结构完全一样。
Write this day down in the guest book: Graham praised a printed page!
「把今天记在访客登记本上：格雷厄姆居然称赞了一张打印纸！」 加上 down 这个小词，把写字变成了“记录在案”，在结构
Write this day down
中，动词的过去式
praised
则表示赞扬或夸奖。
Do not celebrate too much, boss. Paper books still win when it rains.
「别高兴得太早，老板。下雨的时候，还是纸质书管用。」 带着他一贯的冷幽默，格雷厄姆用
Do not celebrate too much
这种自然的方式说出了“别高兴得太早”，给大伙儿的兴奋劲降了降温。
Look at the courtyard clock: half past five! Let us light the lanterns!
「看看庭院里的钟：五点半了！我们点亮灯笼吧！」 用传统方式来表达半点时间，
half past five
字面意思就是“过了五点的半个小时”。现在，用自然语速把整个场景再听一遍吧。
For fifteen years in my hands, that board only held hooks one through eight.
And look on the right edge: there were two tiny screw holes under the varnish all along.
No way! Hook number nine used to hang right there thirty years ago!
One turn, two turns... solid brass hook number nine, back where it belongs.
May I hang the big sunroom key on it, Graham?
Go right ahead, Hannah. You earned it this week.
Wait, Graham, what is that laminated card tucked inside your paper ledger?
Aha! Did you secretly keep a copy of my printed cafe menu, Graham?!
Only because your big numbers are easy to read without a lamp.
Write this day down in the guest book: Graham praised a printed page!
Do not celebrate too much, boss. Paper books still win when it rains.
Look at the courtyard clock: half past five! Let us light the lanterns!
九号黄铜挂钩重新回到了木板上，连格雷厄姆也把汉娜打印的菜单夹在了笔记本里。我们下个场景的庭院见！
Catch you later!
